name: Sports climax
desc: The last minute. Everything is decided.

shots.desc: standing over the ball, one boot resting on it, head lowered, eyes downcast, jaw set, torn dirt-stained jersey, sweat-soaked hair, medium shot, floodlights behind
running start toward the ball, planting foot, body coiled, arms out for balance, torn jersey, motion lines, full body, low angle
leaping mid-air volley, boot striking the ball, torn jersey, hair whipping, speed lines, motion blur, dynamic angle, full body
the ball hitting the back of the net, net stretching and rippling, floodlight glare, close-up, no humans

why: The structure is silence, wind-up, impact, proof. hold_silent buys the stillness that makes the sakuga land - the loudest moment in a short is the one with a quiet shot in front of it, which is why this template spends over a third of its runtime on a man doing nothing. The insert exists because the net, not the striker, is what tells the audience it went in; cutting to a face there would ask the model to act, and it cannot. day_for_night carries the darkness in the ffmpeg grade rather than the prompt, so the floodlit night is actually dark instead of merely described as dark, and wear 4 keeps the damage of the preceding ninety minutes visible on the body.
note: Picture, shot timing, the day_for_night grade and the cue all land today. Two parts do not: `transition: flash` is decorative - short.py hard-cuts every join regardless - and the `determined` emotion contributes its face/eyes/mouth/body tags but its voice_style only applies on TTS engines that accept an emotion vector. Every shot desc reinforces the torn jersey rather than staying silent on it, because wear 4 loses to any earlier, more specific garment tag.
